user.title: Connect to Fleet
user.description: Connect Home Assistant to your Fleet server using a read-only API token.

data_description.url: The base URL of your Fleet server, including the scheme and any port.
data_description.api_token: Create a dedicated API-only user with the Observer role (fleetctl user create --api-only) and paste its token here. API-only tokens are not invalidated when you log out of the Fleet web UI.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only if your Fleet server uses a self-signed certificate.

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authenticate with Fleet
reauth_confirm.description: Fleet has rejected the stored API token for {url}. Enter a new token to reconnect.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure Fleet
reconfigure.description: Update the connection settings for this Fleet server. Use this to rotate the API token before revoking the old one.

data_description.url: Must still point at the same Fleet server.
data_description.api_token: Paste the replacement API-only user token.
data_description.verify_ssl: Turn this off only if your Fleet server uses a self-signed certificate.

error.cannot_connect: Could not reach the Fleet server. Check the URL, that Home Assistant can route to it, and the SSL setting.
error.unknown: Unexpected error. Check the Home Assistant logs for details.

abort.already_configured: This Fleet server is already configured.
abort.wrong_server: That URL points at a different Fleet server. To connect to a different server, add it as a new integration instead.

init.title: Fleet options
init.description: Fleet host status and policy counts only refresh as fast as your osquery agents check in, so polling faster than about a minute rarely surfaces anything new. This fleet currently has {host_count} hosts.

data.missing_after_hours: Treat a host as missing after

data_description.summary_interval: How often to poll Fleet for host counts and policy compliance, in seconds.
data_description.redact_hostnames_in_diagnostics: Replace your Fleet server's hostname in diagnostics downloads. The API token is always redacted.
data_description.inventory_interval: How often to poll the host list and vulnerable software, in seconds. This is the expensive call, so keep it well above the update interval.
data_description.per_host_entities: Creates a device and several entities for every enrolled host. On by default for fleets of 50 hosts or fewer.
data_description.missing_after_hours: How long a host may go without checking in before its missing sensor turns on and a host-missing event fires. Independent of Fleet's own 30-day missing bucket.
data_description.vulnerability_sensors: Track how many software titles have known vulnerabilities.
data_description.label_sensors: One sensor per Fleet label showing how many hosts match it. Fleet's own built-in labels are created but disabled, since several are always empty and All Hosts just restates the total.
